faq.q: What is the maximum group size for a Marbella boat rental in 2041?
faq.a: The maximum is 12 passengers per charter across our fleet, including larger yachts like the Ferretti 94 (29m) and Canados 86 (26m). Smaller boats have lower limits: Dubhe (8m) takes 5 passengers, Mariah SX21 (6.4m) takes 5, and Bandido (11.5m) takes 8. The skipper and any additional crew are not counted in the passenger limit.

faq.q: Is the group size limit the same for all boats?
faq.a: No. Each boat has a specific passenger capacity based on its length, design, and safety certification. For example, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m) holds 9 passengers, the Azimut 39 (12.5m) holds 11, and the Mangusta 80 (24m) holds 12. Always check the individual boat page or contact us via WhatsApp to confirm the limit for your chosen vessel.

faq.q: Does the skipper count in the group size limit?
faq.a: No. The licensed skipper and any additional crew (e.g., host or deckhand) are not included in the passenger limit. So a boat with a 12-passenger capacity can actually accommodate up to 13 or 14 people on board including crew. This is standard practice under Spanish maritime regulations.

faq.q: Can I rent a boat for a larger group, say 20 people?
faq.a: Not from our fleet. Spanish law caps passenger numbers at 12 per boat for most recreational charters. For groups larger than 12, you would need to charter multiple boats simultaneously. We can help coordinate this—contact us via WhatsApp to discuss options for splitting your group across two or more vessels.

faq.q: What happens if my group exceeds the boat's capacity?
faq.a: We strictly enforce passenger limits for safety and legal compliance. If your group is larger than the boat's capacity, we will recommend a larger boat from our fleet (e.g., upgrading from an Azimut 39 to a Mangusta 80) or suggest splitting into multiple charters. Overloading is not permitted and will result in cancellation without refund.

faq.q: Are children included in the passenger count?
faq.a: Yes, every person on board, including infants and children, counts towards the passenger limit. There are no exceptions. Life jackets and safety equipment are provided for all ages. For families with young children, we recommend boats with more deck space and shade, like the Azimut 58 Flybridge or Lagoon 380 catamaran.

faq.q: What is the smallest boat for a group of 10?
faq.a: For 10 passengers, the most suitable options are the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax), Fairline Targa 12m (12m, 10 pax), Lagoon 380 (11.6m, 10 pax), and Pershing 46 (14m, 10 pax). The Azimut 39 (12.5m) holds 11 passengers, so it also works for 10. Always confirm exact capacity at booking.

faq.q: Do I need to book in advance for a specific group size?
faq.a: Yes, especially during peak season (June–September). We recommend booking at least 2–4 weeks ahead for groups of 8–12. Smaller groups (up to 5) can often book with 1–2 weeks' notice. All bookings require WhatsApp confirmation to verify boat availability and passenger count. No walk-up bookings are accepted.

data.body_html:
Planning a group day out on the water in Marbella? Understanding Marbella boat rental group size limits 2041 is essential before you book. Spanish maritime law caps passenger numbers per vessel, and our entire fleet—from the compact Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) to the flagship Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax)—follows strict safety regulations. All charters depart from Puerto Banús, and every booking includes a licensed skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and IVA. Here’s what you need to know to match your group size with the perfect boat.

Why Group Size Limits Matter

Group size limits aren’t arbitrary—they’re set by Spanish authorities based on each boat’s length, stability, and safety equipment. Exceeding them invalidates insurance and can lead to fines or charter cancellation. For 2041, the rules remain unchanged: maximum 12 passengers per charter, plus crew. Our boats range from 5 to 12 passenger capacity, so you’ll always find a fit.

How to Choose the Right Boat for Your Group

Start with your headcount. For groups of 5 or fewer, the Dubhe or Mariah SX21 are budget-friendly options. For 6–8 guests, consider the Bandido or Red Tide. Groups of 9–11 should look at the Astondoa 40, Azimut 39, or Fairline Targa. For a full party of 12, any of the larger yachts (Mangusta 80, Azimut 58 Flybridge, Ferretti 94) work perfectly. Browse our full fleet to compare features and pricing.

Pricing Based on Group Size

Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) cost €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours—ideal for groups of 9–11. The Mangusta 80 (both white and grey variants) starts at €4,719 for a minimum 4-hour charter and includes a free jet ski. For all other boats, pricing is on request via WhatsApp—we’ll tailor a quote to your group size and duration.

What’s Included in Every Charter

Every booking includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden fees. The skipper handles navigation and safety, so you can focus on enjoying the Costa del Sol coastline—from Marbella’s Golden Mile to Cabopino and Estepona.

Tips for Large Groups (10–12 Passengers)

If you’re chartering for 10–12 people, book early—especially between June and September. Boats like the Azimut 58 Flybridge and Mangusta 80 are popular and limited in availability. Consider a full-day charter (8 hours) to visit Cala del Faro, Cala Cortés, or even Sotogrande. For groups exceeding 12, we can arrange multiple boats. Contact us via WhatsApp to plan.
